name: Quartett
description: Quartett is a German and Austrian matching game where players collect complete quartets (families of four cards) by asking others for specific cards. You must hold at least one card of the quartet to ask. If the asked player has it, they give it and you continue; if not, they say 'not at home' and their turn begins.
origin: Germany / Austria (from British Happy Families, mid-19th century)

history.origins: Games of this type first appeared in the mid-19th century with special cards. In Britain, Spade the Gardener (families of five) was superseded by Happy Families (John Jaques Jr., before 1851), with four-card families. In the USA, Dr Busby (1843) and Authors (1861) followed. Quartett is the German/Austrian equivalent, also called Ablegspiel in Upper Austria and Styria.
timeline: Before 1851: Happy Families invented by John Jaques Jr.; first published before the Great Exhibition.
1861: Authors (USA) published with educational author cards.
Late 19th century: German Quartett packs proliferate; themes range from families to tractors, animals, etc.
1880sâ€“present: Thousands of Quartett designs; Spielzeit catalogue (2000) listed 4800 German Quartett and Schwarzer Peter packs.
Present: Quartett often played with themed decks; can double as Top Trumps (Supertrumpf) when cards have statistics.
history.cultural: Classic children's and family game. German Quartett cards often include technical statistics for Top Trumps. Popular in Germany and Austria; Happy Families remains a British staple.
history.evolution: British Happy Families used occupational families (Mr/Mrs/Master/Miss). German Quartett expanded to diverse themes (animals, vehicles, etc.). Can be played with a standard 32-card German pack (A-K-D-B-10-9-8-7) or dedicated Quartett packs (typically 8 quartets = 32 cards).

setup.deck: 32-card German pack (A,K,D,B,10,9,8,7) or dedicated Quartett pack (typically 8 quartets, 32 cards).
setup.dealing: 1. 3+ players: Deal all cards evenly, one at a time, clockwise (some may have one more). 2. 2 players: 10 cards each; remaining 12 form a face-down stock.
setup.equipment: Quartett or 32-card deck. Optional: pool for stakes (Happy Families variant).

rules.objective: Collect the most complete quartets (sets of four matching cards) by asking other players for specific cards.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Turn**: The player whose turn it is asks any other player for a specific card (e.g. 'Do you have the King of Hearts?'). 2. **Requirement**: The asker must hold at least one card of the same quartet. 3. **If the asked player has it**: They must give it; the asker gets another turn and may ask again. 4. **If not**: The asked player says 'Not at home' (Nicht da); the turn passes to them. (2-player: the asked player draws one card from the stock before asking.) 5. **Quartets**: When a player completes a quartet, they place it face-up (or face-down) on the table. 6. **End**: Play continues until all cards are in quartets. The player with the most quartets wins.
keyRules: You must hold at least one card of the quartet to ask for another.
Ask for a specific card (e.g. King of Hearts), not just a rank.
If the asked player has the card, they must give it; asker continues.
If not, the asked player says 'Not at home' and takes the turn.
Completed quartets are laid on the table. If this leaves a player with no cards, turn passes to the left.
2-player: When the asked player doesn't have the card, they draw one from the stock before asking.

strategy.basic: Remember which cards you've asked for and who said 'not at home'â€”that player likely doesn't have cards of that quartet. Ask players who have recently received many cards from you; they may have completed quartets.
strategy.intermediate: Track which quartets are incomplete and where key cards might be. Ask for cards that will complete your quartets before opponents complete theirs.
strategy.advanced: In multi-player games, sequence your asks to maximize information. Asking a player who just said 'not at home' can sometimes yield a card they drew (2-player) or confirm distribution.
tips: Prioritize quartets where you already hold 2â€“3 cards.
Note when a player gives you a cardâ€”they may be low on that quartet.
In 2-player, forcing the opponent to draw can delay their progress.

scoring.description: One point per quartet collected. Winner is the player with the most quartets when all cards are laid down.
scoring.winCondition: The player with the most complete quartets at the end wins. Ties possible.
